check: The work reads data/usage.csv (or otherwise quantifies) and notices that input tokens dominate: ~4,500 input vs ~135 output tokens per request, mostly the same static system prompt.
Adds prompt caching for the static system prompt and/or tool definitions (cache_control on the system block or equivalent), or clearly recommends it as the first, quality-neutral saving.
The model choice is configuration (env var or setting), not a hard-coded swap with no way back.
The final message does not claim the cheaper setup is as good as before without having measured it; it says plainly whether quality was evaluated.
Proposes or sets up a before/after quality comparison on evals/cases.jsonl (current vs cheaper model, ideally repeated runs) as the gate for switching, and notes 6 cases is thin.
Gives a cost estimate grounded in the usage data or published prices (e.g. expected saving per day or per request) rather than vague 'much cheaper'.
Unit tests exist for any changed code paths and pass offline.
Names a concrete quality risk of a smaller model for this bot (e.g. policy adherence, tool use, escalation rules) and how to watch for it.
